items.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: And Gleason was — the boss, George Sosson, that was his name, was a heck of a nice guy and he used have master of ceremonies.

ctx.x: Well those acts probably appreciated when they could come in and give you the music.

Yeah. And we’d rehearse them. Yeah we could read. I had a good piano player, especially like for singers that wanted a little ad lib just piano you know, and then we’d come in on the second chorus with the full band. It was great. It was a great experience. And Gleason was — the boss, George Sosson, that was his name, was a heck of a nice guy and he used have master of ceremonies. He used to go into New York and get acts. It was all usually a dance team, a girl singer, and an emcee — a master of ceremonies. But…
So he did stand up comedy.
